=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:1221-1240, 1310-1348 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The new logic in `single_pass_gate` reads the PR comments, re-enters, and then calculates the next cycle number without serializing these actions, so two concurrent review runs on the same PR can calculate the same "next free cycle" and post markers with that same number.
  WHY: The reviewer marked this SEVERITY: MAJOR. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash said they would not re-flag it, because it is a race that existed before this PR, the previous editor round accepted it as residual, and the changelog and agents.d fragments document it.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "3. Never reuse a cycle number. A status=failed or status=pending marker is not posted with a cycle number that a trusted marker on the PR already carries."
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh, between single_pass_next_free_cycle (cycle selection at lines 1566-1571) and the failed/pending marker posts at lines 1627, 1641, 1663, and 1671; alternatively, serialize the applicable per-PR workflow path in .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: `single_pass_next_free_cycle` (around lines 439-443) computes `max(candidate, highest cycle + 1)` from one comments view, with no atomic reservation, per-PR serialization or recheck before posting. The deterministic-skip-merge job invokes this gate and has no per-PR concurrency group; the per-PR group at review_autofix.yml lines 342-344 applies only to the separate gate job. The agents.d fragment and changelog acknowledge the race ("pre-existing race, narrowed but not closed"), but the issue does not defer the requirement. `test_marker_cycle_number_is_never_reused` only exercises a single gate run. Reviewers disagreed on severity: gemini and openai said MAJOR, minimax said NIT. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash reported no task gaps.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
(No findings reported.)
- HARDENING: scripts/gh_helpers.sh:_gh_pr_cache_note_source, the line `printf '%s %s\n' "$1" "${2:-$(date +%s)}" > "${GH_PR_CACHED_READ_SOURCE_FILE}" 2>/dev/null || true`
  PROBLEM: Bash applies redirections left to right, so if the target file cannot be opened, the "No such file or directory" error goes to the caller's stderr before `2>/dev/null` takes effect. The read itself still succeeds, but a stray error line shows up in the collect step's log.
  WHY: Suggested fix: `{ printf '%s %s\n' "$1" "${2:-$(date +%s)}" > "${GH_PR_CACHED_READ_SOURCE_FILE}"; } 2>/dev/null || true` (1 line).
- HARDENING: scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:single_pass_view_log, `IFS=":"` followed by `for view_path_dir in ${PATH}; do` and then `IFS="${view_old_ifs}"`
  PROBLEM: The unquoted `${PATH}` is subject to pathname expansion, and IFS is changed globally rather than in function scope.
  WHY: Suggested fix: `local IFS=":"` plus `read -r -a view_path_dirs <<< "${PATH}"`, then loop over `"${view_path_dirs[@]}"` (4 lines).
- NOTE: The race in single_pass_next_free_cycle, lines 439-443, was deliberately not re-flagged: it existed before this PR, was accepted as residual, and is documented. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
